subject: Request: Quarterly invoicing + Net-90 pilot for NexaHealth
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nexahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Quarterly invoicing + Net-90 pilot for Redwood contract

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement had a quick follow-up: NexaHealth is requesting a pilot for quarterly invoicing with Net-90 payment terms for the upcoming integration project. This is a standard cadence for our enterprise customers on annual contracts and helps our internal AP cycles.

Can Redwood accept quarterly invoices (one invoice per quarter for the contracted amount) and Net-90 payment terms for the first 12 months of the agreement? We can provide a purchase order template and a short supplier risk form.

I've attached the Nexa PO template and a payment-terms request spreadsheet. If there's a finance or legal process required, please advise what information you need. Tom (CFO) is copied on this thread.

Best,
Sara
Sara Patel
Senior Procurement Manager, NexaHealth
Attachments: Nexa_PO_Template.pdf, nexa_payment_terms_request.xlsx
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Quarterly invoicing + Net-90 pilot for Redwood contract

Sara — thanks for the note and for sharing the templates.

Marissa / Aditya — looping you in for deal desk and revenue ops context. High level: customer asks for quarterly invoices + Net-90 for 12 months. They are enterprise-sized and signed for the initial committed capacity; this is a payment cadence exception rather than a discount request.

From an account perspective we want to be helpful (reduces friction on their side), but we need finance and legal signoff on:
- Credit exposure for Net-90 (finance)
- Invoice format and acceptance criteria for quarterly invoices (revops)
- Contract language for payment term modifications and any late fees or interest (legal)

Can finance do a quick risk check and advise on required mitigations? Ideally we can offer this as a 12-month pilot with a PO and the CFO on record (Tom copied). If needed we can require an initial deposit or milestone-based partial payment.

Olga
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:36:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Quarterly invoicing + Net-90 pilot for Redwood contract

Thanks Olga — flagging commercial implications. A few notes:
- This is acceptable for deal retention in my view, but we should protect revenue recognition and AR risk.
- Suggest we do the following as an offer to Nexa:
  1) Quarterly invoicing for 4 quarters (one invoice per quarter) with Net-90 on receipts, AND
  2) A 30% upfront deposit on the first invoice or an irrevocable PO referencing payment schedule OR
  3) If PO-only, we ask for a credit hold release clause after successful processing of first invoice.

If finance signs off on credit exposure, I'm comfortable moving forward and will prepare the commercial amendment for legal to redline. Marcus — can you run exposure on a $420k ARR committed run rate and confirm whether an upfront deposit is required or we can accept PO-only?

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 10:18:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Request: Quarterly invoicing + Net-90 pilot for Redwood contract

Marissa / Olga — ran the quick numbers and risks (see attached risk_assessment_finance_q1.xlsx).

Summary:
- At $420k ARR the max quarter invoice is ~$105k. Net-90 increases DSO materially and our working capital exposure by ~60 days compared to Net-30.
- Conditional approval options:
  A) Accept quarterly invoices + Net-90 for 12 months if Nexa provides either a 30% deposit on the first invoice OR an Irrevocable PO referencing the Net-90 cadence plus a credit review trigger after Q1.
  B) If neither is acceptable, we can offer Net-60 with no deposit as a compromise.

Operational conditions: require AR to set the invoice terms in our ERP and RevOps to confirm invoice format. Also want CFO email confirmation on the PO cadence (Tom's note).

Attachments: risk_assessment_finance_q1.xlsx

If you want I can approve the PO-only path provided legal sets a short-term security clause and we add an auto-revert to Net-30 if payments are >45 days late on two consecutive invoices.

Marcus Lin
Director of Finance, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@nexahealth.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@nexahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Quarterly invoicing + Net-90 pilot for Redwood contract

All — legal has a brief set of redlines to support the finance-approved path. Two points:
1) Contract amendment language: we will add an Addendum specifying: quarterly invoice cadence, Net-90 terms for the first 12 months, and an explicit reversion clause to Net-30 if two consecutive invoices are >45 days overdue.
2) Security for AR: acceptable forms are (a) 30% initial deposit, (b) Irrevocable PO referencing the Net-90 cadence plus CFO confirmation email, or (c) an approved supplier credit agreement.

I have prepared a redlined contract (attached: contract_redline_nexa.docx). If Nexa confirms (Tom's email) that they can provide an irrevocable PO with CFO on record, and they accept the reversion clause, legal will approve and we can route to DocuSign.

Sara / Tom — can you confirm which of the three security options you prefer? If it's the irrevocable PO route, please attach it and Tom's confirmation; we'll take it from there.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: contract_redline_nexa.docx
